newsitem.title: CANADA: Methanex sees production up by 1 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Methanex sees production up by 1 mln tonnes.

text.p: Methanex Corp expects methanol production of about five-and-a-half million tonnes from its various plants in 1997, president and chief executive Pierre Choquette said on Tuesday.

"(For 1997) production from our units, the current plan is around five-and-a-half million tonnes. That's an increase of about a million tonnes compared to last year," Choquette told a post-earnings conference call.
He said capital requirements this year will probably total about US$95 million to US$105 million, rising to US$275 million in 1998.

"For 1997, US$35 (million) of sustaining (expenditures), US$30 to US$40 (million) to complete Chile Two and then looking at Chile Three, and just having talked to our people in Chile this morning, probably no more than US$30 million for Chile Three in 1997," Choquette said.

Choquette said the forecast production level for 1997 assumes that all the plants are operating at capacity and that the company goes through with its previously announced plan to reduce capacity in Alberta.

Methanex posted better-than-expected fourth quarter earnings before a US$93.4 million writedown on plant and equipment. In the fourth quarter, Methanex's pre-charge net earnings for the fourth quarter were US$0.20 per share.
After the writedown, Methanex lost US$0.30 a share versus a profit of US$0.03 per share in the prior-year period.
Choquette told analysts that the second plant in Chile should have a big impact on Methanex in terms of cost savings.
He said the company's cash cost per tonne of methanol should be under US$100 in 1997.
"Cash costs (including variable costs, fixed costs and the cost of getting the methanol to the customer) should be around US$97 to US$98 per tonne. That's the cash cost per tonne," Choquette said.
"When I said US$97 to US$98 (a tonne), that excluded the amortization of catalysts which is about US$3 (per tonne)," he added later in the call.
